title: Dataset splits: transductive vs inductive
blurb: Why random splits fail, graph-aware splitting

hook.title: Exam leakage among friends
hook.text: Usually you randomly split students into a training set and a test set. But on a graph, nodes are *friends*: if a test student's friends are all in the training set, their answers leak into the test student's embedding. Graph datasets need a careful rule. **Transductive**: everyone is present at both times (you see the full class roster and friendships) but you hide some students' *answers* until test time. **Inductive**: split the friendship graph into separate classes; the test class is one you have never seen.
hook.recall: Remember friends leaking exam answers: nodes aren’t independent. Transductive = same graph, split the labels. Inductive = break the edges, test on unseen graphs.

explore.intro: Six nodes. Flip between the settings and between training and validation time.
tasks: Transductive: at validation time which nodes does the GNN see? Which labels are used?
explore.takeaway: Transductive: one graph, entire graph visible, only labels split (node/edge tasks). Inductive: multiple graphs, edges between splits broken, each split sees only its own graph (node/edge/graph tasks); graph classification only makes sense inductively.
